Package hadur2.core.duel

Class DuelController

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.duel.DuelController
public final class DuelController extends Object
The Duel strand's brain (A2): everything Hadur does against one opponent, lifted out of HadurCore as it stood, to stand beside the melee brain. It is the duel subsystems' owner: the guns, the surf, the waves and state logs, the energy ledger, the shield, the S4 opening and its seeds, the S5 and S6 policies, the rammer and mirror responses, and Duress.

It never decides which role drives, whom to focus on among several opponents, or whether a bullet outcome is its own: the conductor's Duel seam answers those and passes the answers in. It imports nothing from the melee brain; what a melee hands over arrives as a Baton. Its shelves, the .hp library and the survivors' 1v1 profiles read in a melee battle, are handed to it by the conductor by charter, or none.

Per tick the conductor offers it the tick's events one at a time, then asks it to drive if the Duel is the driving role. A scan's radar lock is held until drive(hadur2.core.model.BotInput, hadur2.core.model.BotOrders.Builder, int, boolean), which writes it before the main body's own orders, exactly where the scan wrote it before A2.

    • resumeAfterDuress

      public void resumeAfterDuress()
      RES-14: duress has ended. The waves of both managers, and the per-wave state that goes with them (the gun's virtual bullets, the surf's wave and our bullets' shadows), are from before an interval that went unobserved: processed on the next scan they would be judged against it. They are discarded, and the duel's view of the enemy starts afresh; what the battle learned (the gun's and surf's trees, the ratings, the battle's hit rates) stays.

    • scan

      public void scan(BotInput in, BotEvent.Scan e)
      The scan of the Duel's opponent, after switchOpponent(java.lang.String) (and, on a hand-off, after take(hadur2.core.model.BotInput, hadur2.core.model.Baton, java.lang.String, double)). It drives the duel for this tick:
      • both robots' states are logged, with the KNN features they feed (acceleration, time since the last velocity change, distance moved over the last 8, 20 and 40 ticks);
      • the bullet power is chosen (the gun's rule, raised by POW-1 or POW-2), and a gun wave from us toward the enemy is made at that power, and the gun waves the enemy has crossed are broken to teach the gun;
      • a movement wave from the enemy toward us is made at a guessed power, a candidate for the enemy's next shot;
      • the energy ledger reads the enemy's energy; a corrected drop in [0.1, 3.0] marks the matching movement wave as a real, surfable one (WAVE-1, WAVE-2);
      • the radar lock is held for drive(hadur2.core.model.BotInput, hadur2.core.model.BotOrders.Builder, int, boolean).

    • duressScan

      public void duressScan(BotInput in, BotEvent.Scan e)
      RES-9: a scan in duress only moves where the enemy is thought to be. Everything the normal scan feeds (the state logs, both waves, the ledger, the gun's and the surf's trees) is skipped, since none of it can finish in the time the engine allows.

    • bulletHit

      public void bulletHit(BotEvent.BulletHit e, boolean ownOutcome, boolean foreign, boolean driving)
      One of our bullets hit a robot. Its shadow goes (MOVE-1); a duel bullet's outcome goes to the shield detector and our window; and, if it hit the duel's enemy, the ledger is told the damage it did so that drop is not read as a shot (WAVE-1).
      Parameters:
      ownOutcome - WORLD-5: the outcome is a Duel bullet's and the robot hit is the Duel's
      foreign - the robot hit is outside the duel (a sentry, or not the focus)
      driving - whether the Duel drove this tick

    • hitByBullet

      public void hitByBullet(BotInput in, BotEvent.HitByBullet e, boolean driving, boolean shooterDead)
      An enemy bullet hit us. For the duel's enemy the ledger books its refund of 3 x power (WAVE-1), the wave that carried the bullet is found and logged as a hit for the surf's danger views, and the profile records the hit.
      Parameters:
      driving - whether the Duel drove this tick
      shooterDead - whether the shooter died earlier this round

    • bulletHitBullet

      public void bulletHitBullet(BotInput in, BotEvent.BulletHitBullet e, boolean ownOutcome)
      One of our bullets met an enemy bullet: both are gone. Ours counts as a miss in our window and as an intercept for the shield detector (SHIELD-1); the enemy's wave is marked, so when it breaks it is left out of their hit rate and their rolling window: its bullet never reached us, hit or miss.
      Parameters:
      ownOutcome - WORLD-5: the outcome is a Duel bullet's

    • take

      public void take(BotInput in, Baton baton, String survivor, double survivorEnergy)
      MMEM-2: takes the melee's baton inside the survivor's first duel scan, after switchOpponent(java.lang.String) and before scan(hadur2.core.model.BotInput, hadur2.core.model.BotEvent.Scan). The survivor's recorded shots still short of Hadur become firing waves (a failure is a FAULT record, never fatal), and its 1v1 profile, read and never written, sets the duel's opening.
      Parameters:
      in - the tick's input
      baton - what the melee handed over; null when it could not be made
      survivor - the survivor's name
      survivorEnergy - its energy at this scan
